    # For each pair of consecutive rows, check if there's a path through non-7 cells
    def has_horizontal_path(r1, r2, left_limit=-50, right_limit=20):
        """Check if any path connects (r1,c) to (r2,c) through non-7 cells"""
        if r1 >= r2:
            return True
            
        start_val = demo_input[r1][c]
        
        # Try going up/down first
        curr_r, curr_c = r1 + 1, c
        
        while (curr_r != r2 or curr_c != c) and 0 <= curr_r < 11 and 0 <= curr_c < 17:
            val = demo_input[curr_r][curr_c]
            
            # If we hit background, stop
            if val == 1:

            # Move toward target
            dr = r2 - curr_r
            dc = c - curr_c
            
            if abs(dr) >= abs(dc):

            else:

        return curr_r == r2 and curr_c == c

# Test theory: A column survives IF ALL its bottom markers are reachable from row 6
# via vertical adjacency to OTHER markers in the same column

def can_reach_row_6(markers_list):
    """Check if all markers in list can reach row 6 going down/up"""
    # Get sorted markers
    marks = sorted(markers_list)
    
    # Check connectivity: all should form ONE connected component including row 6
    if not marks:
        return False
        
    first = marks[0]
    last = marks[-1]
    
    # Row 6 should be included
    if first != 6:
        return False
    
    # All markers should be connected to row 6 through adjacent markers
    for i in range(1, len(marks)):
        curr = marks[i-1]
        next_m = marks[i]
        
        # Adjacent means difference <= 1
        if next_m > curr + 1:
            # There's a gap that breaks connectivity
            # Only valid if gap is exactly 1 (one empty row)
            if next_m != curr + 2:
                return False
            else:
                # Gap of 1 is okay - just skip the empty row
                pass
    
    return True

print("=== Testing connectivity theory ===")

for c in range(17):
    sixes_in = [r for r in range(6, 11) if demo_input[r][c] == 6]
    
    if not sixes_in:
        continue
        
    # Check if connectivity holds
    is_connected = can_reach_row_6(sixes_in)
    
    out_sixes = [r for r in range(6, 11) if demo_output[r][c] == 6]
    survived_any = any(out_sixes)
    
    status = "S" if survived_any else "X"
    print(f"Col {c}: sixes={sixes_in}, is_connected={is_connected}, output_kept={out_sixes}")
